_schema.applies_to: matcher on {program, metrics, subgroups}; null = any
_schema.basis: traceability: EFO March 2026 documentation, a GitHub issue, or a measured diagnostic in this repo's data

annotations.text: policyengine-uk calibrates program totals to official spending statistics that are themselves inputs to (or outputs of) the OBR forecast round — where a pe-uk calibration target derives from the same DWP/HMRC outturns or EFO lines, the comparison is consumed_as_target, not held-out validation. Classify per benefit before scoring; the 2024-25 outturn column is the highest-risk year for this. Same boundary rule as the CBO-baseline lane's pre-verified rows.
annotations.basis: cbo-baseline lane note (317 consumed_as_target); policyengine-uk calibration target registry; scorecard issue #37

annotations.text: These are post-measures March 2026 EFO figures: current law plus policy announced by 2026-03-03, on the OBR's March 2026 economy forecast. A PE counterpart must state its own baseline vintage; comparing against a PE run with later policy (or different uprating assumptions) conflates baseline and model differences. Each EFO round is a distinct baseline_key — never treat a newer EFO as a revision of this one.
annotations.basis: EFO March 2026; #21 baseline_key lesson; scorecard issue #13

annotations.text: 2024-25 is outturn (administrative data); 2025-26 to 2030-31 are forecast. Score outturn comparisons as model-vs-admin and forecast comparisons as forecast-vs-forecast — they are different claim types with different expected error.

Universal credit appears in both the welfare-cap and outside-cap sections: the cap excludes spending associated with the jobseeking conditionality group. A PE UC aggregate is the SUM of the two variants; comparing PE UC spending against either variant alone understates. The same applies to DWP social security subtotals.
annotations.basis: Welfare cap definition (Charter for Budget Responsibility); Table 4.9 structure

annotations.text: DWP benefit lines are Great Britain; Northern Ireland's mirror social security is the aggregate 'ni_social_security' rows; HMRC-administered lines (child benefit, tax credits, tax-free childcare, statutory payments) are UK-wide. A UK-wide PE aggregate for a DWP benefit must add the NI share or restrict the simulation to GB.
annotations.basis: EFO expenditure documentation; welfare cap coverage

annotations.text: The incapacity-benefits line excludes the UC health element (footnote 2): legacy ESA/IB/SDA plus the incapacity part of income support only. PE health-related spending built on UC must not be compared to this line; Table 4.11 (health- and disability-related welfare) is the right future counterpart for the combined concept.

Figures are National Accounts expenditure (AME), including payments to people abroad and fraud/error, on an accrual basis. PE simulated entitlement on resident households will structurally undershoot benefits with large non-resident caseloads (state pension) or overshoot where take-up is below PE's calibrated rates. Decompose before diagnosing.

Table 4.9 is NESTED, and rows carry that structure in 'aggregate_level' ('component' | 'subtotal' | 'total') and 'parent'. 'dwp_social_security' is not a program: it is the SUM of the components naming it as parent, and 'other_dwp' in the welfare-cap section is a further subtotal inside it. Any aggregation must filter to aggregate_level == 'component' (or add subtotals only). Summing every non-total row of the in-cap section for 2025-26 gives £319.85bn against the published cap total of £169.13bn — a 1.89x double-count. A PE counterpart mapping must not attach a PE program to a subtotal row.
annotations.basis: Table 4.9 'of which:' markers and cell indentation; components verified to reproduce each published parent to float64 exactness in all seven years by sources/obr-welfare/adapter.py
